newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin says employment priority, reforms gradual.
newsitem.headline: Jospin says employment priority, reforms gradual.

text.p: French Socialist leader Lionel Jospin said on Tuesday that France needed to breathe new life into its economy and make boosting employment a priority.
But he said the Socialist party had learned the lessons of the past and would not implement reforms too quickly, which might only force an about-turn and a new bout of austerity.
In a television interview, he said that France's next government must "give a boost to the economy...with employment as the priority."
France's combined left led the ruling centre-right in the first round of voting in a parliamentary election last Sunday. The second round is due on Sunday.
Jospin reiterated that a Socialist-led government would neither increase taxes nor public spending.
It would plan its reforms over the normal five-year lifetime of parliament.

"Let us learn the lessons of the past," he said, in an apparent reference to the disastrous early years of Socialist government after 1981 when late president Francois Mitterand become France's first Socialist head of state.
"We will carry them out gradually," Jospin said.

The Socialist party has said it would tackle unemployment, running at a record 12.8 percent, by creating 700,000 jobs, half of them in the public sector, and cutting the working week without any loss of pay.
